story_ideas.title: CMS refreshed dataset: Medical Equipment Suppliers
story_ideas.headline: Look up who is listed to supply a walker, a hospital bed or oxygen in your county
story_ideas.angle: A county-level read of the Medical Equipment Suppliers file refreshed 09/06/26, written for people arranging equipment for a parent coming home from the hospital.
story_ideas.hook: The file is the only public list of who Medicare recognizes as a supplier, and it is broken to states and counties.
story_ideas.consumer: Before you accept the first supplier a discharge planner names, check the file for your county and see how many others are listed, then ask each what they carry and what you would owe.
story_ideas.b2b: For suppliers and post-acute discharge teams, the same file shows where local competition is thin and where referral relationships are effectively sole-source.
story_ideas.localize: Breaks down to US states, US counties — rank the outliers.
story_ideas.competitive: Reference data — a refreshed file, so no coverage claim applies either way.
story_ideas.why: If you do not know how many suppliers serve your county, you cannot tell whether the price and wait you are quoted are the only ones available.
story_ideas.note: Reference file, not an event. Localizable to states and counties, so it supports a map or a thinnest-coverage ranking.

story_ideas.title: Medicare Program; Town Hall Meeting on the Fiscal Year 2028 Applications for New Technology Add-On Payments
story_ideas.headline: The technology Medicare pays for in 2028 is being argued over this week
story_ideas.angle: An explainer on what the New Technology Add-On Payment town hall notice dated 09/08/26 decides, for readers who wonder why a new treatment is covered in one place and not another.
story_ideas.hook: The notice is dated two days ahead of this run and concerns applications for fiscal year 2028, so the process is open rather than finished.
story_ideas.consumer: If a doctor has mentioned a newer device or treatment, this is the process that determines whether Medicare adds payment for it, and the meeting notice tells you when the discussion happens.
story_ideas.b2b: Device makers and hospital finance teams read the applications list as a forecast of which technologies will carry add-on payment two fiscal years out.
story_ideas.chart: The underlying file supports an original ranking or trend line.
story_ideas.competitive: Monitored trades cover this beat and have not written it.
story_ideas.why: Knowing the pathway exists is the difference between assuming a new treatment will never be covered and tracking the point at which it might be.
story_ideas.note: Confirmed gap: monitored publishers cover this beat and none matched the notice.

story_ideas.title: Medicare Program; Regulatory Alignment for Predictable and Immediate Device (RAPID) Coverage Pathway
story_ideas.headline: A faster route from device approval to Medicare coverage
story_ideas.angle: A plain-language piece on what the RAPID coverage pathway notice published 08/11/26 changes about the wait between a device reaching market and Medicare paying for it, for patients and the clinicians who prescribe.
story_ideas.hook: The pathway's name states its own premise, predictable and immediate coverage, and no monitored publisher has matched the notice.
story_ideas.consumer: If you have been told a device is approved but not covered, this notice describes the mechanism meant to shorten that gap.
story_ideas.b2b: Manufacturers and provider finance teams need to know which submissions this pathway takes and what it does to the revenue timeline on a new device.
story_ideas.why: The lag between approval and coverage is often what a patient actually pays for out of pocket, and this is the rule aimed at it.
story_ideas.note: Confirmed gap. National in scope, pairs naturally with the equipment supplier file for a two-part story.

feature_pitch_raw:
**The pattern:** Medicare spent the past month rewriting how a new device gets paid for, and the only public record of who would actually supply one refreshed on the same calendar. The Federal Register carries the Regulatory Alignment for Predictable and Immediate Device (RAPID) Coverage Pathway notice (08/11/26), the Alternative Payment Model incentive payment advisory requesting current billing information from qualifying APM participants (08/13/26), and a town hall meeting notice on the Fiscal Year 2028 applications for New Technology Add-On Payments (09/08/26). CMS reposted its Medical Equipment Suppliers file on 09/06/26, broken to states and counties. Read together, these are the two ends of one pipeline: Washington is deciding now which technology Medicare will pay for in 2028, and the supplier file is the only place a patient can see whether anyone near them is listed to hand it over. The three pitches before this one (09/03, 09/04, 09/05) all sat on the CMS nursing home files against BLS staffing; this run's unwritten thread is the device and equipment side of the same agency.

**Why it matters:** A coverage decision made in a hearing room in 2026 reaches an older adult only through a supplier who is listed in their county, and the Medical Equipment Suppliers file is the record that shows whether one is. For people managing oxygen, mobility equipment or home monitoring, the distance between a national payment pathway and a local supplier list is the whole story, and nothing in these notices tells them which counties are thin. The stake is concrete but bounded: three notices set the terms for what gets covered, one county-level file shows who can deliver it, and no monitored publisher has matched any of the three notices.

**Why pitch this now:** The town hall notice is dated 09/08/26, two days ahead of this run, and it is about applications for fiscal year 2028, so the window for anyone wanting to follow the process is open right now rather than after a rule lands. The RAPID pathway notice published 08/11/26 and the APM billing information request 08/13/26 sit in the same month. The supplier file refreshed 09/06/26, giving a reporter a current county-level cut to pair against them.

**Angle:** Whether Medicare's newer, faster routes to paying for technology reach patients in counties where hardly any supplier is listed to provide it. Working title: "What Medicare Pays For Next." For payer and provider policy readers, and for the families who buy the equipment.

**Potential headlines:**
- Medicare is deciding now what technology it pays for in 2028
- The supplier list is the last mile of every Medicare device decision
- Three notices, one town hall, and the equipment your parent needs at home

- **Fierce Healthcare** — covers Medicare coverage pathways and payment policy for readers who follow NTAP and APM decisions as they happen, not after the fact.
- **Modern Healthcare** — the RAPID pathway and the APM billing request are national payment-policy shifts with business consequences for device makers and provider groups.
- **SeniorLiving.org** — its readers are the ones checking whether a supplier is listed in their county before ordering equipment.
- **Bankrate Retirement** — connects the coverage decision to what an older household ends up paying out of pocket for equipment.
